Deficits in working memory (WM) are linked to alterations in prefrontal theta\u2013gamma cross-frequency coupling. Low-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) has emerged as a non-invasive, low-cost approach capable of modulating ongoing oscillations in targeted brain areas through entrainment. This study investigates the impact of multi-session peak-coupled theta\u2013gamma cross-frequency tACS administered to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) on WM performance in older adults. In a randomized, sham-controlled, triple-blinded design, 77 participants underwent 16 stimulation sessions over six weeks while performing\n                    <jats:italic>n<\/jats:italic>\n                    -back tasks. Signal detection measures revealed increased 2-back sensitivity and robust modulations of response bias, indicating improved WM and decision-making adaptations, respectively. No effects were observed in the 1-back condition, emphasizing dependencies on cognitive load. Repeated tACS reinforces behavioral changes, indicated by increasing effect sizes. This study supports prior research correlating prefrontal theta\u2013gamma coupling with WM processes and provides unique insights into the neurocognitive benefits of repeated tACS intervention. The well-tolerated and highly effective multi-session tACS intervention among the elderly underscores its therapeutic potential in vulnerable populations.\n                  <\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1007\/s11357-024-01272-3","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2024,7,11]],"date-time":"2024-07-11T21:01:54Z","timestamp":1720731714000},"page":"1425-1440","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1007\/springer_crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":32,"title":["Boosting working memory in the elderly: driving prefrontal theta\u2013gamma coupling via repeated neuromodulation"],"prefix":"10.1007","volume":"47","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0009-1726-1040","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Lukas","family":"Diedrich","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Hannah I.","family":"Kolhoff","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Clara","family":"Bergmann","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Mathias","family":"B\u00e4hr","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Andrea","family":"Antal","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"297","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2024,7,12]]},"reference":[{"key":"1272_CR1","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","first-page":"101337","DOI":"10.1016\/j.eclinm.2022.101337","volume":"45","author":"PP Velandia","year":"2022","unstructured":"Velandia PP, Miller-Petrie MK, Chen C, et al.
